mainTopic: Searching garments for lost stains and lost כלאים, מצוות בטלות לעתיד לבוא, Torah-level שעטנז, stains on colored garments, and the seven substances for testing a stain
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא on searching a garment for a lost stain. You check it section by section, and a section is at least three fingerbreadths. Lost semen is found with a needle in a new garment and by sunlight in a worn one. A ברייתא then rules that a garment with lost כלאים may be used as תכריכין, and רב יוסף learns from this that מצוות בטלות לעתיד לבוא. When challenged with רבי ינאי, he answers with רבי יוחנן, who allows even burial in it, since the dead are free from מצוות. רב חסדא rules that dyeing such a garment permits it, based on a משנה about searching until bedrock. מר זוטרא permits a cloak when we are unsure whether a linen thread was fully pulled out, because Torah-level שעטנז needs combing, spinning and weaving together, and the הלכה follows him over רב אשי. A ברייתא then argues over whether a stain on a colored garment makes a woman impure, and the גמרא explains that colored garments were almost banned during Vespasian's war. Finally, a new משנה begins listing seven substances used to test a stain.

steps.title: Search the garment section by section
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that a garment in which a blood stain got lost is checked one section at a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: He checks it section by section.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its ruling about a garment where a blood stain got lost: you look through it piece by piece until you find the stain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since nobody knows where the stain is, a quick glance is not enough. Checking one small area at a time makes sure no part of the garment is missed.

keyTerms.meaning: Section by section, one area at a time

phrases.english: He examines it section by section.
phrases.notes: 'It' is a garment where a blood stain got lost; this teaching starts just before this line.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא about a garment with a lost stain, which began just before this line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A garment with a lost stain must be checked section by section.

steps.title: How to find lost semen in a garment
steps.stepSummary: If semen got lost in a garment, a new garment is checked with a needle and a worn-out one is checked by holding it up to the sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: If semen got lost in it: if the garment is new, he checks it with a needle. If it is worn out, he checks it in the sun.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second case. Semen that got lost in a garment is searched for differently depending on whether the garment is new or worn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a new, thick garment you can feel the spot by poking it with a needle. In a worn, thin garment the sunlight shines through, but not through the stained spot, so the stain shows up.

phrases.english: If semen was lost in it,
if it is new, he examines it with a needle,
if it is worn out, he examines it in the sun.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel case of something lost in a garment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lost semen is found with a needle in a new garment and by sunlight in a worn one.

steps.title: How big is a 'section'?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines the 'section' from step 1 as at least three fingerbreadths.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: a 'section' is not less than three fingerbreadths.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא explains the word 'section' used in step 1, so we know how big each area to check should be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a size, 'section by section' would be unclear. The minimum of three fingerbreadths gives the checking a fixed measure.

keyTerms.meaning: A section or area of the garment

phrases.english: It was taught: A 'section' is not
less than three fingerbreadths.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: אֵין שְׁכוּנָה פְּחוּתָה מִשְּׁלֹשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines a term from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A section for checking is at least three fingerbreadths.

steps.title: A garment with lost כלאים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a garment with a lost thread of כלאים may not be sold to a גוי or made into a saddlecloth, but it may be made into תכריכין for a dead person.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: a garment in which כלאים got lost may not be sold to a גוי and may not be made into a donkey's saddlecloth. But it may be made into burial shrouds for a dead person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another case of something 'lost' in a garment: a forbidden wool-linen thread whose location is unknown. It lists what you may and may not do with such a garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the forbidden thread cannot be found and removed, the garment is treated with caution. A Jew might end up wearing it, so selling it or using it for a donkey is forbidden. Using it as a shroud for the dead is allowed, and this permission sets up רב יוסף's inference in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden mixture of wool and linen (שעטנז)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A garment in which diverse kinds were lost —
phrases.notes: Someone sewed a wool thread into linen, or the reverse, and now nobody knows where it is.

phrases.english: he may not sell it to a gentile,
and he may not make it into a saddlecloth for a donkey,
but he may make it into shrouds for a dead person.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בֶּגֶד שֶׁאָבַד בּוֹ כִּלְאַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא with a similar theme: something lost in a garment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A garment with lost כלאים may not be sold to a גוי or used as a saddlecloth, but may be used for תכריכין.

steps.title: רב יוסף: מצוות will be cancelled in the future
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף infers from the shroud permission that מצוות are cancelled לעתיד לבוא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This shows that the מצוות will be cancelled in the time to come.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף draws a big principle out of the small ruling about shrouds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At תחיית המתים the dead will rise wearing their shrouds. If the איסור of כלאים still applied then, burying someone in כלאים would be a problem. Since the ברייתא allows it, רב יוסף concludes that מצוות will no longer be in force at that time.

keyTerms.meaning: This shows, we can learn from this
In the future, at the time of תחיית המתים

steps.whyThisMatters: This statement, 'מצוות בטלות לעתיד לבוא,' becomes a well-known principle that is quoted in many places.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: That is to say —
the מצוות will be nullified in the future.
phrases.notes: Otherwise, the dead would rise at תחיית המתים still wearing a forbidden כלאים garment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general principle from the ברייתא in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מצוות will be cancelled לעתיד לבוא.

steps.title: Challenge: allowed only for the eulogy, not for burial
steps.stepSummary: אביי (or רב דימי) objects that, according to רבי ינאי, the כלאים shroud is allowed only during the הספד and not for burial.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him (some say it was רב דימי): But didn't רבי מני say in the name of רבי ינאי that the ruling applies only to eulogizing him, but burying him in it is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's proof by limiting the ברייתא to the הספד only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the dead person may not be buried in the כלאים shroud, then nobody will rise wearing it. So the ברייתא proves nothing about מצוות being cancelled in the future, and רב יוסף's inference falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (another version of who said it)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי, וְאִי תֵימָא רַב דִּימִי:
phrases.english: Abaye said to him, and some say Rav Dimi:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי מָנִי אֲמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי,
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Mani say that Rabbi Yannai said:
They taught this only for eulogizing him,
but burying him in it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי מָנִי אֲמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's inference in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's proof that מצוות בטלות לעתיד לבוא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the shroud is allowed only for the הספד and not for burial, the dead will not rise in it, so there is no proof.

steps.title: Answer: רבי יוחנן allows it even for burial
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that רבי יוחנן ruled the כלאים shroud is allowed even for burial, so the proof stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Wasn't it stated about this that רבי יוחנן said it is allowed even for burying him?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends his inference by quoting רבי יוחנן, who disagrees with רבי ינאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף relies on רבי יוחנן's opinion that burial in the כלאים shroud is allowed. Then the dead really will rise wearing it, so the ruling still shows that מצוות are cancelled in the future.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא allows a כלאים garment as תכריכין. רב יוסף learns from this that מצוות בטלות לעתיד לבוא. The challenge from רבי ינאי (only for the הספד) is answered with רבי יוחנן, who allows it even for burial.

phrases.english: He said to him: Wasn't it stated about it:
Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Even to bury him.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו אִיתְּמַר עֲלַהּ, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relies on a different אמורא who disagrees with the source of the challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following רבי ינאי, burial in כלאים is forbidden, so the proof fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: Following רבי יוחנן, burial is allowed too, so רב יוסף's inference stands.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's ruling fits his teaching that the dead are free from מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן's permission to bury in כלאים matches his own reading of the פסוק 'במתים חפשי': once a person dies, he is free from the מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן is consistent with his own view. He said: What does the פסוק 'free among the dead' mean? Once a person dies, he becomes free from the מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the previous answer by showing that רבי יוחנן's ruling about the כלאים shroud comes from a larger principle he taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7, רב יוסף quoted רבי יוחנן that a כלאים shroud is allowed even for burial. Here we see why: רבי יוחנן reads 'במתים חפשי' to mean a dead person has no more מצוות. That explains why the dead may wear כלאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning; consistent with his known view
He becomes free from the מצוות

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, once a person dies he is free from the מצוות. That is why a כלאים shroud is allowed even for burial.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle that the dead are free from מצוות supports רב יוסף's broader claim in step 5 about מצוות and the dead.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan follows his own reasoning,
for Rabbi Yochanan said:
What is meant by what is written: "Free among the dead"?
Once a person dies,
he becomes free from the מצוות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 7 by showing the principle behind רבי יוחנן's ruling
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a כלאים shroud is allowed even for burial
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's reading of the פסוק 'במתים חפשי'

steps.title: A garment with a lost כלאים thread may be dyed and then worn
steps.stepSummary: רפרם בר פפא quotes רב חסדא: if a כלאים thread got lost in a garment, you can dye the garment, and then it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם בר פפא said in the name of רב חסדא: A garment in which כלאים got lost: one dyes it, and it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ruling about a garment with a lost forbidden thread: dye it and then it may be worn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, step 4 said a garment with a lost כלאים thread may not be sold to a גוי. Now רב חסדא gives a way to fix the problem. Dyeing helps because, as the next steps explain, wool and linen take dye differently, so a hidden thread would show.

keyTerms.meaning: A forbidden mix, here wool and linen together in one garment (שעטנז)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא, אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rafram bar Pappa said that Rav Chisda said:
A garment in which diverse kinds were lost,
one dyes it, and it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא, אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: how to deal with a garment where a כלאים thread was lost
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dyeing a garment with a lost כלאים thread makes it permitted to wear

steps.title: רבא asks where רב חסדא got this rule
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רפרם בר פפא what source רב חסדא, 'the elder', has for allowing a dyed garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רפרם בר פפא: Where does the elder get this from?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks for the source of רב חסדא's ruling. This sets up the next step, where the source is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא is not attacking the rule. He wants to know what earlier teaching it is based on, since it seems surprising to rely on dyeing to decide that the forbidden thread is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know this? A request for a source
The elder; here a respectful name for רב חסדא

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rava said to Rafram bar Pappa:
From where does the Elder get this?
phrases.notes: "The Elder" means רב חסדא, whose ruling רפרם just quoted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling in step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The earlier source behind רב חסדא's rule that dyeing makes the garment permitted

steps.title: The source is the משנה about searching until bedrock
steps.stepSummary: רפרם answers that the rule comes from a משנה: someone searching a pile for buried impurity digs until bedrock, and if nothing is found we say a raven took it. So too, wool and linen take dye differently, so if no difference shows, we say the thread fell out.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is a משנה, as we learned: One searches until he reaches bedrock, and if nothing is there, we say a raven took it. So too here: wool and linen together do not take the dye the same way. Since no difference is seen, we say the thread fell out.
steps.whatsHappening: רפרם gives רב חסדא's source by comparing the garment to a משנה about searching for a lost source of impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, once a proper search finds nothing, we may assume the impure item is gone, even though we do not know where it went. The same goes for the garment: dyeing is a proper search, because a linen thread would show up as a different color. If the whole garment dyes evenly, we assume the thread fell out.

keyTerms.meaning: He searches until he reaches bedrock
A raven took it; a way to explain why something is gone

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is not about clothing at all. It is about impurity buried under a pile of stones. רפרם is only borrowing its logic: once a proper search finds nothing, we may assume the thing is gone.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is a mishna,
as we learned: One searches until he reaches bedrock,
phrases.notes: This משנה is about a pile of stones known to have something impure buried under it.

phrases.english: and if it is not there, say a raven took it.
So too here:

phrases.aramaic: עַמְרָא וְכִיתָּנָא בַּהֲדָדֵי לָא סָלֵיק לְהוּ צִבְעָא,
phrases.english: wool and linen do not take dye the same way,
and since no difference is noticed,
say it surely fell out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question from step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב חסדא learned from the משנה that after a proper search finds nothing, we assume the item is gone. Dyeing is that search for the garment.

steps.title: A linen thread pulled out of a wool cloak, unsure if fully removed
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא rules that if someone sewed a linen thread into a wool cloak and pulled it out, but is unsure whether all of it came out, the cloak is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב ייבא said in the name of מר זוטרא: Someone who put a linen thread into his wool cloak and pulled it out, and does not know whether it all came out or not, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ruling about כלאים: a cloak is permitted when we are unsure whether a linen thread was fully removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the person already took action to remove the forbidden thread. Only a doubt remains about whether a bit stayed behind. מר זוטרא rules that this doubt does not forbid the cloak.
steps.whatToRemember: A garment with a possible leftover כלאים thread can be permitted: by dyeing it and seeing no difference (רב חסדא), or when the thread was pulled out and only a doubt remains (מר זוטרא).

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יֵיבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּמָר זוּטְרָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rav Yeiva said in the name of Mar Zutra:
One who put a thread of linen
into his wool cloak and pulled it out,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא יָדַע אִי נְתִיק אִי לָא נְתִיק —
phrases.english: and does not know whether it was fully pulled out or not,
it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יֵיבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּמָר זוּטְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related ruling about a doubtful leftover כלאים thread
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a linen thread was pulled out of a wool cloak and it is unclear whether all of it came out, the cloak is permitted

steps.title: Why is מר זוטרא lenient?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind מר זוטרא's ruling that the cloak is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why מר זוטרא allowed the cloak even though some linen thread might still be inside. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, if you are unsure whether something forbidden is still there, you might expect to be strict. The גמרא wants to know what makes this case different.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means: why is מר זוטרא lenient in Step 12, when we don't know if all the thread came out?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind מר זוטרא's ruling in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The basis for being lenient about a doubtful remaining linen thread.

steps.title: Sewing alone is only a rabbinic ban, so a doubt is permitted
steps.stepSummary: By Torah law, שעטנז requires combing, spinning and weaving together. Sewing is only a rabbinic ban, so in a case of doubt the cloak is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: By Torah law it is written 'שעטנז': it is not forbidden until it is combed (שוע), spun (טווי) and woven (נוז). The רבנן are the ones who made a גזירה about sewing. Since he does not know whether he pulled it all out, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the Torah word שעטנז is read as three parts: combed, spun and woven. Just sewing a thread in is only forbidden מדרבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sewn-in thread is not combed, spun or woven together with the wool, so the Torah does not forbid it. The ban comes only from the רבנן, and when a doubt involves a rabbinic ban we can be lenient. That is why the cloak is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah word for a forbidden mixture of wool and linen, read here as שוע, טווי, נוז

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key rule: when the Torah itself does not forbid something and only the רבנן do, a doubt can be treated leniently.

phrases.english: By Torah law, 'שעטנז' is written
meaning it is not forbidden until it is combed, spun, and woven.
phrases.notes: The word שעטנז is split into three pieces: שוע, טווי, נוז.

phrases.english: And it is the רבנן who made a decree about it,
phrases.notes: He means the רבנן forbade just sewing or attaching wool and linen together.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵיוָן דְּלָא יָדַע אִי נַתְּקֵיהּ — שְׁרֵי.
phrases.english: and since he does not know whether he pulled it all out, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Sewing wool and linen together is only a rabbinic ban, because Torah-level שעטנז needs combing, spinning and weaving. So a doubt is permitted.

steps.title: רב אשי: maybe any one of the three is enough
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges the reading: maybe the Torah forbids wool and linen that are either combed, or spun, or woven.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objects: Say instead that it means either combed, or spun, or woven!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks the reading from Step 14. He suggests that each of the three actions might be enough on its own to make it forbidden by Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If any one action is enough, the ban may be stronger than just a rabbinic decree, and the reason for being lenient falls apart. So רב אשי is questioning the base of מר זוטרא's leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it (a strong challenge)

phrases.english: רב אשי objects to it:

phrases.aramaic: אֵימַר אוֹ שׁוּעַ אוֹ טְוִוי אוֹ נוּז!
phrases.english: Say it means either combed, or spun, or woven!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of שעטנז given in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that שעטנז requires all three actions together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The three parts of the word might be alternatives, each one forbidden by itself, and not requirements that must all be present.

steps.title: The הלכה follows מר זוטרא
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows מר זוטרא, because the Torah put all three into one single word.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is like מר זוטרא, since the Merciful One expressed them in one word.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules like מר זוטרא and rejects רב אשי's reading. Its proof is that the Torah wrote all three ideas together as one word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since שעטנז is a single word, the three parts belong together: combed AND spun AND woven. So Torah-level שעטנז needs all three, sewing is only a rabbinic ban, and the doubtful cloak is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Merciful One', meaning God, in the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: Torah-level שעטנז needs wool and linen combed, spun and woven together, because it is one word. Sewing alone is a rabbinic ban, so if you are unsure a thread is still there, the garment is permitted.

phrases.english: And the הלכה is in accordance with מר זוטרא,
since the Merciful One expressed them in one word.
phrases.notes: The one word is שעטנז, so all three parts go together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אשי's challenge and rules like מר זוטרא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows מר זוטרא: שעטנז needs all three actions, so a doubtful sewn thread does not forbid the cloak.

steps.title: תנא קמא: a colored garment makes her impure because of a כתם
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא opens a new topic. The first opinion says a stain on a colored garment makes a woman impure as a כתם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A colored garment makes impure because of a כתם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא about blood stains. The first opinion says that if a woman finds a stain on a colored garment, she becomes impure because of the כתם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here a colored garment is treated just like any other garment when it comes to stains. This sets up the argument with רבי נתן בר יוסף in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A blood stain found on a garment or body, which can make a woman impure

phrases.english: The רבנן taught:
A colored garment makes impure because of a stain.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בֶּגֶד צָבוּעַ מְטַמֵּא מִשּׁוּם כֶּתֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic. It connects loosely to the earlier talk of dyed garments in Steps 9-11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stain on a colored garment makes a woman impure as a כתם.

steps.title: רבי נתן בר יוסף: a colored garment does not make her impure
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן בר יוסף disagrees. A colored garment does not make her impure, because colored garments for women were set up to be lenient about stains.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן בר יוסף says: It does not make impure because of a כתם, since colored garments for a woman were only enacted to be lenient about their stains.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן בר יוסף argues on the first opinion. He says a stain on a colored garment does not make her impure, and he gives a reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reason is that colored clothing for women exists only to make things easier for them with stains. If a colored garment still made her impure, that purpose would be lost.

phrases.english: רבי נתן בר יוסף says:
It does not make impure because of a stain,
for they did not enact colored garments for a woman
except to be lenient regarding their stains.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing opinion in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stain on a colored garment does not make a woman impure, because colored garments were set up to be lenient about stains.

steps.title: What enactment could there be?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the word 'enacted': what kind of enactment were the רבנן supposed to have made?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Enacted'? What did they enact?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks on רבי נתן בר יוסף's wording. Saying the רבנן 'enacted' colored garments does not make sense, because there was nothing to enact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תקנה is a new rule the רבנן put in place. But women did not need a special rule in order to wear colored clothing, so the word 'enacted' looks wrong.

phrases.english: 'They enacted'? What did they enact?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רבי נתן בר יוסף in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word תקנו in רבי נתן בר יוסף's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wearing colored garments needs no rabbinic enactment, so 'enacted' does not fit.

steps.title: Read it as 'permitted' instead of 'enacted'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords the statement: colored garments were permitted to women only to be lenient about their stains.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: colored garments were permitted to a woman only to be lenient about their stains.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes רבי נתן בר יוסף's wording. Instead of 'enacted', it reads 'permitted'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing the word to 'permitted' removes the problem of what the enactment was. The reason stays the same: it was all to make things easier with stains.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, שֶׁלֹּא הוּתְּרוּ בִּגְדֵי צִבְעוֹנִין לְאִשָּׁה
phrases.english: Rather, colored garments were not permitted to a woman
except to be lenient regarding their stains.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, שֶׁלֹּא הוּתְּרוּ בִּגְדֵי צִבְעוֹנִין לְאִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19 by rewording the statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי נתן בר יוסף speaks of a rabbinic enactment of colored garments.
steps.terutzMaskana: He means colored garments were permitted to women for the sake of leniency about stains.

steps.title: 'Permitted' implies they were once forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new wording: if colored garments were 'permitted', that implies they were forbidden before.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They were permitted'? That implies they were forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks the corrected wording from Step 20. Saying something was 'permitted' suggests it used to be forbidden. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fix created a new problem. We don't know of any time when women were forbidden to wear colored clothes, so 'permitted' also seems hard to explain.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not the end of the discussion. The גמרא asks the question here and answers it right after, so don't conclude that colored clothing was really forbidden.

phrases.english: 'They were permitted' implies that they were forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rewording given in Step 20.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Permitted' implies an earlier ban on colored garments, which does not seem to have existed.

steps.title: Yes, colored garments were almost forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that colored garments really were nearly forbidden. A משנה reports that during Vespasian's war the רבנן banned bridegrooms' crowns and drums and wanted to ban colored garments too. They decided that allowing them was better, so women could be lenient about stains.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true, as we learned in a משנה: During the war of Vespasian, the רבנן made decrees against bridegrooms' crowns and against the drum. They wanted to make a decree against colored garments as well. But they said: It is better to allow them, so that women can be lenient about their stains.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 21 by saying 'Yes.' Colored garments really were close to being banned, and it brings a משנה to show this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that the word 'permitted' suggests colored garments had once been forbidden. The גמרא agrees and shows that during the war of Vespasian the רבנן banned other things and wanted to ban colored garments too. They decided against it because a stain on a colored garment does not make a woman impure, so the word 'permitted' really means 'they chose not to forbid.'

keyTerms.meaning: Crowns that bridegrooms used to wear

steps.whatToRemember: Colored garments were nearly banned during the war of Vespasian. The רבנן kept them permitted because a stain on a colored garment does not make a woman impure, which helps women avoid unnecessary impurity.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the רבנן weighed a decree against its cost in practical הלכה. Here, avoiding needless impurity outweighed the decree.

phrases.english: Yes, as we learned:
In the war of Vespasian
they decreed upon the crowns of bridegrooms
and upon the drum,
they sought to decree upon colored garments.
They said: This is preferable,
phrases.notes: 'This' means letting women keep wearing colored clothing.

phrases.english: in order to be lenient regarding their stains.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21 by accepting its point and supporting it with a משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the implication and supports it with a source from a משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Calling colored garments 'permitted' seemed odd, because nothing suggested they had ever been forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: They were nearly forbidden after Vespasian's war, and the רבנן chose to permit them so women could be lenient about stains.

steps.title: Seven substances used to test a stain
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. It lists seven substances that are rubbed on a stain to check whether it is blood or dye. The first five are tasteless saliva, water from split beans, urine, natron, and בורית.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Seven substances are rubbed on a stain to test it: tasteless saliva, water from split beans, urine, natron, and בורית,
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a new topic. It begins listing seven substances used to test whether a stain is really blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stain could be blood or just dye. Blood comes out when these cleaning substances are rubbed on it, so they help decide whether a stain is blood. The list continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Natron and בורית, two cleaning agents

phrases.english: Mishnah: Seven substances
are applied to the stain:
tasteless saliva, and liquid from split beans,
and urine, and natron, and borit,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the colored-garment discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seven substances are applied to a stain to test whether it is blood. The first five are tasteless saliva, water from split beans, urine, natron, and בורית.
